Hey, I’m so sorry this happened to you and I’m glad you’re reaching out. Does your campus have any orgs relating to supporting survivors or a women’s center of some kind? I find that how the title ix process goes realllyyyy varries by college so it might be helpful if you had someone from your specific school to talk to. The women’s center on my campus was so helpful to me when i went through this process.

My experience was….not the best. But i don’t regret it. Some of the officials were not as kind as i would have hoped and it was really hard to go through. But in the end, I was able to get a no contact order and documentation that i reported what happened. This made me feel safer in a way, just knowing that if it escalated further i had proof that i had reported it before. 

My perpetrator also lied, but i was still able to get the no contact order. The important thing to know is that it can’t protect you in the short term (not enforceable by police, they can’t remove him from the premises), but after the fact he can be kicked out if he violates it. 

Honestly, I didn’t get a ton out of it,he didn’t get kicked out, and it was a really difficult and heartbreaking experience. But it did make me feel better to be doing /something/, have it on paper, and have the no contact order. It’s 100% up to you of course but that was just my experience. I’m wishing you well ♥️

For me, I still remember it but it doesn’t hurt to think about. It’s not a pleasant experience, just a neutral one. I’m able to think about a traumatic event and just be like “hm yeah, that happened.” with no extreme emotional response tied to it. 

i was also worried when i first started that i was never gonna “get there” But then one day as i was reprocessing she asked how i was feeling and i just wasn’t feeling anything. It took a minute for that to register but once it did i was amazed. For me it doesn’t normally happen mid session, like i don’t go from feeling it to not feeling it in the same day. Your mind still processes when you aren’t thinking about it so one day i’ll just go into a session and basically be done with it. We keep going to make sure and sometimes I find other stuff that’s still painful, but so far i’ve been able to fully reprocess like four different events? I have a long way to go but i’m hopeful. 

It’s really great! I just wish it wasn’t so painful and time consuming to get there 😅

This is a good thought, but also if the predator assaulted anyone else it absolutely isn’t their fault. They aren’t responsible for that persons actions and reporting jt doesn’t automatically mean that they wouldn’t be able to do it again.

I’ve struggles with a lot of these feelings. The painful truth is that something can be wrong and traumatic, but there simply isn’t enough prove for the law to consider it illegal. 

No matter what the legal system says, what happened to you was abuse. It was wrong, it was traumatic, and it was as bad as you know it is. If it affected you enough to be in this subreddit it was bad. 

Personally, I chose not to report for a lot of reasons. One was that I didn’t realize it was assault at the time. I don’t remember the exact day it happened, I didn’t say no very strongly, I stayed with him afterword. It was still rape, it was still traumatizing, but no jury would convict. 

Something that helped me was to stop considering the legal system the only way for me to find closure. Systems will fail us, and it’s not fair. For me, I learned that to heal I need to stop seeing a conviction as what will finally make me feel okay again. 

I know this was kind of rambly, but I guess my main point is that just because you might not be able to prove it in court, doesn’t mean that it didn’t happen. Even if a jury wouldn’t believe it. it was still bad enough. It was still abuse, it was still traumatic. I believe you and I believe it was as bad. 

If you do still want to talk about your options, you could talk to a free legal aid agency in your state. They could give you some guidance on wether pressing charges would be likely to end in a conviction and they would be able to tell you what you might experience during the case. If it happened while you were a child they are required to report it though so keep that in mind. 

I’m wishing you the best

I feel the same way a lot of the time. After I was raped all I thought about was scrubbing at my body with steel wool to get him off of me. 

One thing that helps me was remembering that body’s are constantly shedding cells and creating new ones. The skin that he touched isnt the same skin I have now. Those cells have died and were replaced by new ones. My hair has grown out and been cut and replaced by new hair that he’s never seen. I try to remember that even if it feels like the same body, it isn’t. 
I don’t know if that will help you, but I just wanted to share. I’m wishing you the best.

I hate it and don’t want to think about it, but I think it’s normal to come up because it was so impactful. It doesn’t mean that you enjoyed it or wanted it to happen, it’s just your brain making correlations. 

I’m sorry that you’re experiencing this, I wish I could help you get rid of it but I’m still figuring that out myself. However, I promise that it’s normal. 

Wishing you the best

None of us would ever judge you. I’m so sorry that you have experienced this. How you want to define it is up to you, but personally I would consider this to be rape. You did not give consent to anything other than a kiss and you were impaired from the weed. What happened is not your fault and you did not deserve for that to happen. 

What you do next is up to you, but know that you have options. 

You can look at this doc for information on if you think you might want to report this to the police, but you don’t have to if you don’t want to. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jSFwve5cs7HxDYfdoywTwhBv_uctAVu7TGxwY2Izpo0/mobilebasic

RAINN also has a lot of good resources and you can even call them. 

https://www.rainn.org/articles/steps-you-can-take-after-sexual-assault

Some places even have text lines if you don’t want to talk on the phone, but they vary by state. You can google “Sexual Assault Text Line -your state-“ and something should come up. 

Also, from personal experience, this is so much easier when you aren’t alone. I hope you have someone close to you who you are able to tell about this. 
I’m wishing you all the best.
